claims: The API checks don't prove any permission, not just PR write — `scripts/bootstrap/codex-cloud-setup.sh:177-186`: repo is public so both `gh api` calls pass for any valid token; a token without PR write passes setup, then fails later at `gh pr create`
Docs (`docs/notes/codex-cloud-setup.md:29-30, 46-50`) and the commit title say this verifies what shipping needs, but it only checks auth and API reachability
The script grew past the 600-line cap — `codex-cloud-setup.sh` (547 → 609), violating the rule in `docs/pr-checklists/recurring-review-patterns.md:202-204` that it be split in the same PR
The new probes ignore the existing non-GitHub-origin skip — `codex-cloud-setup.sh:556-557`: with such an origin `gh repo view` fails and `set -e` stops setup, so setups that pass today will fail
If `gh` does resolve a repo with a non-GitHub origin, the write probe pushes a branch to whatever `origin` is
Probe branch names can collide across containers (line 192): same PID and same second; on the same commit, the second push silently succeeds and whichever deletes second fails its setup
On a probe branch name collision with different commits, the push is rejected and the error wrongly tells you to grant Contents write
Cleanup trap turned off after a failed delete (lines 217-220): a failed delete leaves the branch behind and fails setup; error should say to delete it manually
Misleading error (`codex-cloud-setup.sh:206-212`): every push failure says to grant Contents read/write, including network errors, branch rules and name collisions
Vercel sees every probe branch: `ui-dashboard/vercel.json` only turns off deployments for `sentry-autofix/*`, so each probe push reaches Vercel's build-skip script
Playwright step (`codex-cloud-setup.sh:530-538`): a failure stops setup, unlike `claude-code-web-setup.sh:140-152` which makes it non-fatal, and it prints no guidance
The docs' outbound-access list (around `docs/notes/codex-cloud-setup.md:68`) leaves out the apt mirrors that `--with-deps` needs
Tests: the delete-failure path and `verify_github_api_capabilities` have no tests

judge_reasoning.3846756487: Review item 1 says the API checks don't prove PR write permission even though the docs claim they do, so a token without PR write passes setup.
judge_reasoning.3846756810: Review item 3 says the new probes lack the non-GitHub-origin guard that verify_origin_git_auth has (lines 158-161).
judge_reasoning.3846756918: Review covers the cleanup trap being disabled after a failed delete and confirms the branch is left behind, though it downgrades severity.
judge_reasoning.3846756922: Review confirms probe branch names can collide across containers because of same-second timestamps and reused PIDs, and suggests a random suffix.
judge_reasoning.3846757143: Review notes side effects of probe branches (Vercel, publishing HEAD) but never flags that the probe mutates origin at all or suggests a non-mutating check like --dry-run.
judge_reasoning.3846757191: Review says the docs' outbound-access list leaves out the apt mirrors that playwright --with-deps needs.

1.why: verify_github_api_capabilities (setup.sh:177-186) only does GETs on repos/{repo} and pulls, so PR write is never checked. That is the known issue at :195 (it only probes PR read access).

2.why: The docs say PR read/write is required but setup only reads PRs, which is the known docs/PR-read issue at :195. The claim's 'only auth and API reachability' is also overstated, since verify_origin_write_access does push a real branch.

3.why: The raw count did go from 547 to 609, but the repo's size tool (file-size-watchlist.mjs statusForCounts, hashComments for .sh) applies the soft cap to non-comment lines. This file has 518 of those, so it is only 'watch', not over the cap.

4.why: verify_github_api_capabilities runs unconditionally after verify_origin_git_auth, which skips non-GitHub origins (lines 158-161). That is the known issue at :179.

5.why: Same root cause as the known :179 issue (the new probes ignore the non-GitHub-origin skip), combined with the known :231 issue that the probe changes the real origin.

6.why: The branch name is codex-cloud-write-probe-$(date +%s)-$$, which can collide. Already covered by the known 'Make the temporary branch name globally unique' at :192.

7.why: This is what happens when the known name collision at :192 occurs. The wrong-remedy part overlaps with claim 9.

8.why: Setting created=false before return 1 turns off the trap cleanup. Already known at :242 and :243 (keep cleanup enabled after a delete failure).

9.why: Any non-zero exit from 'git push origin HEAD:refs/heads/...' prints the fixed heredoc telling you to grant Contents read/write. Failures from rulesets or rejected pushes get the same wrong advice. No known item covers this.

10.why: vercel.json disables deployments only for sentry-autofix/*, so it is true that probe branches reach ignoreCommand. But this is a side effect of the known :231 P3 (the probe creates and deletes a branch on the real origin every run).

11.why: It is true that the Playwright install is fatal, unlike claude-code-web-setup.sh:140-152. But codex-cloud-setup.md:39 says setup fails closed on tool installation, and there is a CODEX_CLOUD_INSTALL_PLAYWRIGHT_DEPS opt-out, so this is a design preference, not a defect.

12.why: The outbound-access list leaves out the distro package sources that --with-deps needs. Already known at docs/notes/codex-cloud-setup.md:70 (document the distribution package source).

13.why: The new test cases in codex-cloud-setup.test.sh cover only playwright on/off, write-probe success and push refused. Nothing tests the delete-failure branch or verify_github_api_capabilities.
